BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER I‑INTRODUCTORY
1. Short title, extent and commencement.‑(1) This
Ordinance may be called the Baluchistan Local Government Ordinance, 1980.
(2) It extends to the whole of the Province of
Baluchistan.
(3) It shall come into force at once except the provisions
of Chapter XVIII which shall come into force with effect from such date as the
Gov ernment may by Notification in the official Gazette specify in this behalf.

Power to exclude an area

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER I‑INTRODUCTORY
2. Powers to exclude an area.‑The Government may by
Notification exempt any area or areas from any or all provisions of this
Ordinance.

Definitions

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER I‑INTRODUCTORY
3. Definitions.‑.In this Ordinance, unless the
context otherwise require‑
(1) `annual rental value' means the gross annual rent at
which a Building or Land may be let from year to year ;
(2) `budget' 'means an official statement of income and
expenditure of a. Local Council for a financial Sear ;
(3) `building' includes any shop, house, hut, outhouse,
shed, stable, en closure wall, wells, verandah, platform, plinth, ramp, stair‑case
and steps ;
(4) `Chairman' means the Chairman of a 'Local Council
constituted under this Ordinance and includes the Mayor of a Municipal
Corporation ;
(5) `Cattle' means cows, buffaloes, bulls, oxen, bullocks,
heifer, calves, camels sheep and goats ;
(6) `City' means an area declared to be a city under this
Ordinance ;
(7) `Conservancy' means the collection, treatment removal
and disposal of refuse ;
(7‑A) "Consumption" means utilization of
an article by causing change in its existing position and nature, which may
include conversion of a ship other floating structure into its pieces, scrape
and other articles of similar nature, commonly known and styled as ship
breaking;
[Added by Ordinance VI of 1982‑Take effect from 1‑7‑1980.

(8) "Dealer" means any person who within a
market area sets up, establishes, or allows any place to be used for the
purchase or sale of farm produce ;
(9) "District" means a revenue district;
(10) "District Council" means District Council
constituted under this Ordinance;
(11) "Divisional Co‑ordination Committee"
means a Committee constituted under this Ordinance.
(12) "Drain" includes a sewer, a house drain,‑
a drain of any other des cription, a tunnel, a culvert, a ditch, a channel and
any other device for carry ing sullage or rain water ;
(13) "Dwelling house" means any building used
substantially for human habitation ;
(14) "Elected member" means a member who has
been elected under the provisions of this Ordinance.
(15) "Erect or re‑erect a building" means
the construction of a new build ing and includes such material alterations of a
budding as enlargement of any wall, verandah, fixed platform, plinth or a part
of the building struc tural conversion of two or more places, for human
habitation or a building not originally meant for the purpose, structural
conversion of two or more places of human habitation into a greater number of
such places, addition of any room, building substance or other structure to a
building, reconstruction of a whole or any part of the external walls of a
building, or the renewal of the parts of a wooden building, construction in a
wall adjoining any street or land, not belonging to the owner of the wall, or
opening of a door to such street or land, such alterations of the internal
arrangements of a building as affect its drainage, ventilation or other
sanitary arrangements or its security or stability ;
(16) "Farm produce" means all agriculture
crops/produces including Live stock produces and hides, skins, woollen and ghee
or any other product derived from any one of these or any other commodity that
may be declared by Notification to be farm produce;
(17) "Food" includes all edibles used for food
or drink by human beings but does not include drugs and water ;
(18) "Government" means the Government of
Baluchistan ;
(19) "Grower" means a person who grows farm
produce personally or through tenant or otherwise ;
(20) "Land" includes land which is being built
up or is built up is cove red with water or is under cultivation or is fallow,
and in relation to Town Improvement Committee includes land as defined in
clause (a) of section' 3 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 ;
(21) "Local. Area" means area under the
jurisdiction of ,a Local Council ;
(22) "Local Council" means a Local Council
constituted under this Ordin ance ;
(23) "Local Court" means the Court constituted
under this Ordinance ;

Repeal and savings

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER I‑INTRODUCTORY
4. Repeal and savings.‑'[(1) The British Baluchistan
Bazar Fund Regu lation, 1910 (V of 1910) in respect of Rural Councils and Town
Committees, and the Baluchistan Local Government Ordinance, 1979 (1X of 1979)
are hereby repealed.]
(2) Where an enactment stands repealed under subsection
(1) any ap pointment, rules, regulations or bye‑laws made or saved,
notification, order or notice issued, tax imposed or assessed, scheme prepared
or executed, contract entered into, suit instituted, rights acquired, claims
made, legal or administrative proceedings or action taken thereunder or under
the Baluchistan Local Government Act, 1975 (XII of 1975) shall so far as it is
not inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance, be deemed to have been
respectively made, saved, issued, imposed or assessed, prepared, or executed,
entered into, instituted, acquired, made or taken under this Ordinance.

Ordinance to override other laws

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER I‑INTRODUCTORY
5. Ordinance to override other laws.‑The provisions
of this Ordinance shall take effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent
therewith contained in any other Law.

Succession

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER I‑INTRODUCTORY
6. successions.‑(I) A District Council shall be the
successor of such District Council which may have been constituted under the
Baluchistan Local Government Ordinance, 1979 hereinafter referred. to as
Ordinance IX of 1979.
(2) A Municipal Committee or a Town Committee shall be the
successor of such a Municipal Committee or a Town Committee which may have been
constituted under Ordinance IX of 1979.

Local areas

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER II‑LOCAL AREAS
7. Local Areas.‑(1) For the purposes of this
Ordinance the Local Area; shall be a Union, Tehsil, District, Town,
Municipality, Mohallah and a City.
(1) Subs. by Ordinance I of 1982.
(2) Government may, by notification, declare any area
urban or rural . other than a Cantonment Board,, as:
(a) A Town.
(b) A Municipality.
(c) A City:
(d) A Union.
(e) A Tehsil, or
(f) A Mohallah.
(3) Government may, by notification in the official Gazette,
specify the name by which the Corporation, Municipal Committee (and Mohallah
Com mittee), Town Committee, District Council, Tehsil Council and Union Council
shall be known and unless the name is so specified it shall be known as the
Municipal Corporation, ‑Municipal Committee (and Mohallah Committee),
Town Committee District Council, Tehsil Council and Union
Council as the case may be, of the place where its office is situated.

The Government may by notification

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER II‑LOCAL AREAS
8. The Government may, by notification:‑
(a) declare any area‑
(i) comprising a revenue estate, not included within a
city, a Munici pality or a Cantonment Area, to be a Union provided that, part
of the revenue estate falls outside the city, the Municipality, Town or
Cantonment area, and may either be declared a Union or may from part of
contiguous revenue estate for the purposes of declaring a Union.
(ii) not included within the Municipality, Cantonment Area
or city, to be a Tehsil and specify names of Unions comprised therein;
(iii) within a Municipality to be a Mohallah;
(iv) not included within a Cantonment Area and which has
developed urban characteristics, to be a Town or Municipality and specify the
extent and limits of such area:
Provided that all Municipalities and Town Committees
constituted under the repealed laws shall, under this Ordinance, constitute
Town Committees, Municipalities, or
(v) constituting a Corporation to be a city;
(b) extend, curtail or otherwise alter the limits of a
local area and declare that any area shall cease to be a Union, Mohallah,
Tehsil, Town, Municipality, or a City as the case may be.

Certain characteristics of local areas

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER II‑LOCAL AREAS
9. Certain characteristics of local area.‑(1) As for
as may be, the local areas declared as Union, Mohallah, Tehsil, Town,
Municipality or a City under this Ordinance may conform to certain
characteristics, namely :‑
(a) the local areas may be a territorial Unity;
(b) the area of Union shall not exceed the. limits of
Tehsil and shall have population between 10,000 to 15,000 and may consist of a
group of contiguous Villages;
(c) the population of a town may vary from, 5,000 to
10,000;
(d) the population of a Municipality may exceed 10
thousand but not one lac;
(e) save as otherwise provided or notified by the
Government a city may comprise a population of one lac or above.
(2) The Government may, for reasons to be recorded, waive
any of the aforesaid characteristics while delimiting the Local areas.

Constitution of local councils

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER III‑CONSTITUTION OP LOCAL COUNCILS
10. Constitution of Local Councils.‑(1) As soon as
may be, the follow ing Local Councils may be constituted‑
(a) a Union Council for each Union;
(b) a Tehsil Council for each Tehsil;
(c) a Town Committee for each Town;
(d) a District Council for each District;
(e) a Municipal Committee for each Municipality; (f) a
Municipal Corporation for each city; and
(g) a Mohallah Committee for each Mohallah.
Explanation.‑The Local Councils, mentioned in sub‑clauses
(a), (b) and (d) shall be called Ruler Councils and those mentioned in sub‑clauses
(c), (e), (f ) and (g) shall be called Urban Councils.
(2) A Local Council shall be a body corporate having
perpetual succes sion and a common-seal with power subject to the provisions of
this Ordinance and the rules, to acquire, hold and transfer property, both
movable and immovable and shall, by its name, sue or be sued.

Division amalgamation and reconstitution of local councils

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER III‑CONSTITUTION OP LOCAL COUNCILS
11. Division, amalgamation and reconstitution of Local
Council.‑(1) Government may, by notification, divide a Local Council into
two or more Local Councils or amalgamate two or more Local Councils into one
Local Council and may specify in the notification consequences which shall
ensue upon the publication of such notification.
(2) When as a result of such division or amalgamation any
new Local Council is constituted in accordance with the provisions of this
Ordinance or in the manner specified in the notification the existing members
of any local council so divided or amalgamated shall become the members of such
Local Council or Local Council as the Government may, by notification, specify
as if such member had been elected to that Local Council.

District councils and union councils

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER IV‑COMPOSITION OF LOCAL COUNCILS
12. Rural Councils, District Councils and Union Councils.‑Subject
to other provisions of this Ordinance, Rural Councils shall be‑
(1) the District Council constituted under this Ordinance,
shall consist of the number of members equal to the Union Councils in the
District which in other words means that one member will or elected from each
Union Council. All elected Chairmen of Tehsil Councils and Town Committee in the
District and all heads of Nation Building Departments in the District will be.
ex officio members of District Council, provided that the members from various
Nation Building Departments shall have no right to vote.
Explanation.‑Nation Building Departments shall
include Agricultural and Livestock, Education, Local Government and Rural
Development, Irrigation and Power, Industries, Health and Social Welfare,
Communication and Works and Co‑operative Department, Revenue Department
and Forest Department and such other Departments of the Provincial Government,
as the Government may notify.
[Added by Ordinance IV of 1981.]
(2) The Tehsil Council constituted under this Ordinance
shall consist of the elected Chairmen of the Union Councils in the Tehsil. All
elected Chairmen of Town Committees and all representatives of Nation Building
Departments at Sub‑Divisional level will be ex officio members of the
Tehsil Council. The official members from various Nation Building Departments
shall have no right to vote.
(3) the Union Council constituted under this Ordinance may
have 9 to 15 members.

Urban councils

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER IV‑COMPOSITION OF LOCAL COUNCILS
13. Urban Councils, Municipal Corporation, Municipal
Committee, Town Committee (and Mohallah Committees).‑The Urban Councils
and number of members of such Councils shall be as follows:‑
(1) Municipal Corporation, 40 to 60 members.
(2) Municipal Committees, 15 to 50 members.
(3) Town Committees, 7 to 13 members.
(4) Mohallah Committees, 5 to 9 members.
Provided that separate seats shall be allocated ‑for
Muslims and non -Muslims member to be elected on the principle of separate
electorate provided further that at an election to a Muslim seat in any local
council only such person shall be entitled to vote in an electoral unit as are
enrolled on the electoral roll prepared on the principle of separate electorate
for such units:
Provided further that the number of` seats for minorities
will be over above the minimum number of seats fixed for the Local Council.

Municipal corporation

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER IV‑COMPOSITION OF LOCAL COUNCILS
14. Municipal Corporation.‑A Municipal Corporation
shall consist of such number of members as may be fixed by Government, ranging
between 40 to 60.

Representation of tenants, Peasants, Worker and Women

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER IV‑COMPOSITION OF LOCAL COUNCILS
15. Representation of tenants, Peasants, Worker and Women.‑(1)
A District Council may have such number of members representing peasants,
tenants, workers and women as may be prescribed and they shall be elected in
the prescribed manner:
Provided that a Local Council other than a District
Council may also have such number of members representing women as may be
prescribed and they shall be elected in the prescribed manner.[ Added by
Ordinance XII of 1981.]
(2) Nothing contained in subsection (1) shall prevent the
members of the special interest mentioned in the said subsection from being
elected to general seat in any District Council.

Representation of tenants workers and women

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
16. Election of Chairman of Local Councils.‑For
every Local Council there shall be a Chairman who shall be elected in the
prescribed manner: provided that the Chairman of Municipal Corporation may be
designated as Mayor.

Chairman

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
17. Election of members of Local Councils.‑(1) Save
as otherwise provided, election of members of all Union and District Councils,
Municipal Corporation, Municipal Committees and Town Committees shall be held
on the basis of adult franchise through secret ballot.
(2) Below the Union Councils/ Municipal Committees there
may be informal bodies at village level in the rural areas to be called village
council or by any other appropriate name or all these bodies would be
constituted on the basis of consensus of residents of the Village and Mohallah
Committees in urban area and not through any formal elections. The procedure
for obtaining such consensus shall be prescribed:
(3) The Electoral
unit may be multi‑member or single member and in any multi‑member
electoral unit the candidates securing the highest number of votes shall be
elected, and
(4) Every voter within an electoral unit shall have only
one vote irrespec tive of the number of the members to be elected from the
electoral unit provided that at an election to a Muslim or a non‑Muslim
seat in any electoral unit only such persons shall be entitled to vote as are
enrolled on the electoral roll prepared on the principle of separate electorate
for such area.

Members of the provincial and national assemblies observes

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
18. Election Authority.‑(1) Government may appoint
an Authority called the "Baluchistan Local Council Election
Authority" for conducting elections to the Local Councils.
(2) Election Authority shall exercise such powers and
perform such functions as may be prescribed.

Election of chairman of local councils

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
19. Electoral Rolls.‑Electoral Rolls prepared for
the general elections of Provincial Assembly as amended from time to time or
the electoral rolls prepared in the prescribed manner shall be the electoral
rolls for elections to the Local Councils.

Qualifications of candidates and members

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
20. Qualifications of candidates and members.‑Any
person who is not less than twenty‑one years of age on the last day fixed
for filing the nomina tion form shall be qualified to be elected as a member of
a Local Council if for the time being his name appears on the electoral rolls
of the local area of that Local Council.

Disqualification of candidates and members

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
21. Disqualification of candidates and members.‑A
person shall be disqualified to be a candidate or a member of a Local Council‑
(a) if he has ceased to be a citizen of Pakistan;
(b) if he is an undischarged insolvent;
(c) if he is of unsound mind and has been so declared by a
competent Court;
(d) he has been on conviction for an offence involving
moral turpitude, sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not less than six
months, unless three years or such less period as Government may, in any case,
specify, has elapsed from the date of expiration of the period of the sentence;
(e) if he is a salaried person in the service of Pakistan
or of a Public statutory corporation, a Local Council or other Local Authority;
and
(f) if he is under contract for work to be done or goods
to be supplied to the Local Council concerned or has otherwise any pecuniary
interest in the affairs of any of the Local Councils in the Province.
(g) if he has been dismissed as public servant within the
meaning of the Pakistan Penal Code (XLV of 1860) and a period of three years
has not elapsed from the date of such dismissal;[ Added by Ordinance XII of
1981.]
(h) if he fails to submit declaration of assets and
liabilities, as required under section .25 within a period of 30 days from the
date he subscribes to an oath, before taking his seat in office;
(i) if he undermines the ideology, security or solidarity
of Pakistan or an conviction for these charges, sentenced to imprisonment for
any term, unless three years or such period as. Government may, in any case,
specify, has elapsed from the date of expiration of the sentence.

Electoral rolls

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
22. Candidate not to contest election on Party basis.‑‑(1)
No candidate contesting election under the provision of this Ordinance, shall
directly or indirectly‑
(a) gives himself out as a candidate or nominee of a
political party.
(b) claim or draw or receive any financial or other
assistance from any political party for the purposes of the elections.
(c) take, display, or carry any document, sign, insignia,
flag or other thing indicating his association with, or affiliation to, any
political party.
(d) seek the vote on the sympathies of the people on party
basis or on the basis of the manifesto of any political party, or
(e) seek the vote or support of the people by attributing
direct or indirect party affiliations to any of his opponents.
(2) whoever‑
(a) is found by the Returning Officer to have contravened
the provisions of subsection (1) shall stand disqualified from being a
candidate for election under this Ordinance for a period of four years.
OR
(b) Having been elected under this Ordinance, if found by
the Authority to have contravened the provisions of subsection (1) shall cease
forthwith to hold the office to which he was elected and stand disqualified from
being a candidate for election under this Ordinance for a period of four years;
Provided that action under clause (a) or (b) of subsection
(2) shall not be taken unless the Returning Officer or the Authority as the
case may be, has issued show‑cause notice and has given the candidate an
opportunity of being heard.

Qualifications of candidates and members

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
23. Conduct of Elections.‑‑(1) Election to
Local Councils shall be con ducted in the prescribed manner on the principle of
separate electorate for Muslim and non‑Muslim seats. .
(2) Election rules and offences.‑The Government may
make rules for carrying out the purposes of this chapter.
(3) Election offences, penalties and procedure are
appended in Seventh Schedule.

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
24. Term of office.‑(I) The term of office of a
Local Council shall be four years commencing on the day on which it assumes
office:
Provided that the first term of office of a Local Council
shall not be less than two years;
Provided further that on the expiry of the term of office
of a Local Council the Government may extend the term of office for a period
not exceeding six months or appoint any person for the like period to perform
such functions of the Local Council as may be specified.
(2) A Local Council shall, in its first meeting and to the
exclusion of any other business, elect from its members a Chairman in the
prescribed manner;
Provided that the first meeting shall be held not later
than thirty days from the day on which the names of its members are notified.

Conduct of elections

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
25. Declaration of assets.‑Every Chairman or member
of Local Council, shall before he enters . upon his office, submit to the
prescribed authority in such manner as the Government may ‑direct, a
declaration‑ in writing or properties, both movable and immovable,
whether within or outside Pakistan, which he or any member of his family owns,
or which he has in his possession or under his control, or in which he or any
member of his family bas any beneficial interest.
Explanation.‑In this section, the expression `member
of his family' in relation to a person, includes‑
(a) the spouse of such person, and
(b) such of the children, parents, as reside with and are
wholly dependent upon such person.

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
26. Oath of office.‑A member/Chairman shall before
taking his seat make and subscribe to an oath in such form as may be
prescribed.

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
27. Bat against double membership.‑(I) No person
shall at the same time be a member of more than one Local Council.
(2) Nothing in subsection (I) shall prevent a person from
being a candi date for two or more seats at the same time whether in the same
Local Council or in different Councils, but if he is elected to more than one
seat he shall, within a period of to (sixty) days after the declaration of the
result for the last such seats, resign all but one of the seats and retain the
seat of his choice and that until he has opted for one of such seats, he shall
not take oath of office in any Local Council in term of section 26.

Oath of office

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
28. Casual vacancy.‑(1) If the Office of a member or
a Chairman for any reason, falls vacant during the term of office of a Local
Council a new member or Chairman as the case may be shall be, elected in the
prescribed manner and he shall hold office for the residue of such term.
(2) If the vacancy in the office of a member occurs within
four months of the expiry of the term of a Local Council the vacancy shall not
be filled.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in subsection (2)
unless the time is extended by the Government, the vacancy in the office of the
Chairman shall be filled within fifteen days from the date such vacancy is
notified.

Casual vacancy

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
29. Removal.‑(1) The Government may, after. giving
him an oppor tunity of being heard, remove a Chairman or a member of a Local
Council from office in the prescribed manner, if he‑
.
(a) has incurred any of the disqualifications enumerated
in sections 21 and 22 ; or
(b) absents himself without reasonable cause from three
consecutive meetings of the Local Council ; or
(c) is guilty of abuse of power or misconduct ; or
(d) refuses to take oath under section 26, or is prevented
from taking oath under subsection (2) of section 27.
Explanation.‑In this subsection misconduct includes
bribery, corruption, jobbery, favouritism, nepotism or wilful diversion of the
funds of the Local Council or any attempt at or abetment of such misconduct.
(2) A Chairman or a member of a Local Council removed
under sub section (1) may submit a representation, within a period of 30 days
from the date of the order of removal, to the Government.[ Subs. by Ordinance
XIX of 1980.]
(3) A Chairman removed from office shall cease to be a
member.

Removal

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
30. Resignation.‑2L(1) A Chairman or a member may
resign his office by tendering resignation in writing to the Government through
the Secretary, Local Government Department with a copy to the Local Council of
which be is the Chairman or member.
[Subs. by Ordinance I of 1982.]
(2) The Administrative Department, on receipt .of the
resignation will proceed under section 34;
Provided that if the Chairman has incurred liability for
removal, it shall, at that stage, reject the resignation and initiate action
for removal.

Resignation

BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
BALUCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1980
CHAPTER V‑ELECTION AND RELATED MATTERS
31. Vote of no‑confidence.‑A Chairman shall
vacate office if a vote of no‑confidence is passed against him in the
prescribed manner by two‑third majority of the total number of members of
the Local Council ; provided that‑
(a) motion of non‑confidence shall not be moved
before the expiry of three months of his assumption of office as Chairman ; and
(b) where a motion of no‑confidence against a
Chairman has been moved and has failed to secure the requisite majority of
votes in its favour at the meeting no similar motion will be moved against him
before the expiry of three months from the date such motion was moved.

39. Meetings.‑(1) The Government may frame rules and
regulations for the conduct of the meeting of the Local Councils meeting which
may, besides other matters provide for :‑
(a) the types of meetings, that is to say, ordinary,
special or emergent ;
(b) the types of business, to be conducted in different
types of meetings ;
(c) the place of meetings ; notices required for different
meetings ;
(e) authority to call meetings ;
(f) notice of agenda for the meetings ;
(g) quorum for different meetings ;
(h) order of the business to be conducted in meetings ;
(i) the manner of asking questions ;
(j) motions. and amendments and their withdrawal or
discussions thereon ;
(k) speeches to be delivered ;
(1) training, discourses or discussions to be arranged at
the meetings ;
(m) maintenance of order/decorum in the meetings ;
(n) provide for decision by votes ;
(o) language to be used ;
(p) adjournments or postponements ;
(q) co‑opting of other members or officials ;
(r) re‑consideration of the matters once disposed of
;
(s) recreational or entertainment programme to be arranged
at the time of meetings ; and
(t) adjustment of meetings.
(2) All meetings of a Local Council shall be presided over
by its Chairman, and in his absence by a member chosen for that purpose by the
members present.
(3) The Local Council shall hold meetings as prescribed
under the rules and regulations framed by the Government.
(4) A Local Council shall hold a general meeting at least
once a year to which all voters of the Local area shall be invited. The notice
of such meet?ing shall be given or publicity made in such manner as the Local
Council may by resolution decide from time to time.
(5) A member of a Local Council shall not be liable to any
proceeding in any Court in respect of anything said by him or any vote given by
him in the meeting of a Local Council or in a Committee, thereof, so long as
such action does not undermine the ideology, integrity or solidarity and
security of Pakistan and does not infringes the Constitutional Fundamental
Rights.
(6) All meetings, shall be open to public except when a
Local Council by majority vote decides to consider any matter in a session
attended exclusively by its members.
(7) Names of the members present and minutes of the
proceedings at each meeting shall be drawn up and recorded in a book to be kept
for the purpose which shall be signed by the person presiding at the meeting
and shall at all reasonable times and without charge be open to inspection by
members, provided that no member shall be entitled to object to the minutes of
any meeting in which he was not present.
(8) All decision in a meeting of a Local Council shall be
taken by majority of votes of the members present provided that the Presiding
Authority may have a casting vote in case of equality of votes.
(9) A member, who directly or indirectly, by himself or by
any partner, employer or employee has any share or interest in respect of any
matter or has acted professionally in relation to any matter on behalf of any
person having therein any such share or interest as aforesaid, shall not vote
or take any part in any proceedings relating to a matter as aforesaid of a
Local Council or any of its Committees.

which were made, taken or done, or purported to have been made, taken or done,

notifications, rules, orders, or bye‑laws made thereunder shall be deemed
to have been validly made, taken or done.

all authorities and all officers who immediately before the enforcement of this
Ordinance were exercising functions of Local Councils under the repealed enactments
or any other law shall continue to exercise their respective functions till the
Local Councils are constituted under this Ordinance, provided Government may
withdraw all or any of the functions from such authorities or officers as it
may deem necessary.

CHAPTER XXIII‑BYE‑LAWS
166.‑(1) A Local Council or Market Committee may,
and if required by Government shall make bye‑laws not inconsistent with
this Ordinance and the rules framed thereunder to carry out the purposes of
this Ordinance.
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality
of the foregoing powers, such bye‑laws may provide for all or any of the
matters specifically required to be provided by bye‑laws, enumerated in
Sixth Schedule, under this Ordinance and the matter incidental, consequential
and supplemental thereto.
(3) The bye‑laws shall take effect subject to the
approval of she Govern ment.
(4) The Government may modify the bye‑laws or return
the same to the Local Council or the Market Committee for being reframed.
(5) The bye‑laws as approved by the Government shall
be published in the official Gazette and shall take effect from such date as
prescribed by the Government.
(6) The Government may cancel the bye‑laws and
thereupon the bye‑laws shall cease to have effect.
